home.title: Umut Yüksel
content: I am a Research Fellow at the Department of Political Science at University College London and Research Associate at the Global Governance Centre of the Geneva Graduate Institute. Before joining UCL, I was a Marie Skłodowska-Curie fellow at the Department of Political and Social Sciences at Universitat Pompeu Fabra. I obtained my PhD (summa cum laude) from the Geneva Graduate Institute in November 2019 with a thesis entitled “Bargaining Over Maritime Boundaries in Times of Legal Uncertainty”. Prior to this, I held a pre-doctoral fellowship at the Department of Political Science at Stanford University with the support of the Swiss National Science Foundation, and visiting research fellowships at Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals, the Centre of Excellence for International Courts and Governance at the University of Copenhagen (iCourts), the Faculty of Law at Universitat Pompeu Fabra, and the Department of International Relations at Bilkent University. My research interests lie at the intersection of international security, international organizations, international law, and domestic politics. Using original data and mixed-methods, I examine how characteristics of international law and domestic political institutions shape the claims that states make and the ways in which they manage their disputes. I work on these queries in various domains, ranging from sovereignty to trade and human rights.

If you are interested in my work, want to exchange views or collaborate, I would be more than happy to talk to you. research.title: Research — Umut Yüksel
content: My recent project (Beyond Maximalism: The Role of Domestic Political Institutions in the Making and Reception of Excessive State Claims [CLAIMAX]), supported by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, investigated the ways in which domestic political institutions influences the making and reception of maximalist state claims. The project-related documents, working papers, and data will be shared in a separate section on this website in due course. More generally, my research lies at the intersection of international security, international law, and domestic politics. I rely on original data to examine the determinants of state claims and disputes, focusing on domestic political institutions and international law. You can find some of my work below: PublicationsThe Domain of International Adjudication: Why Sovereign States Abandon Decision Control (with Fuad Zarbiyev) (under contract with the Cambridge University Press)The LaGrand Effect: Changes in the Demand and Supply of ICJ Provisional Measures (with Phattharaphong Saengkrai), Journal of International Dispute Settlement (online first)The Law Behind Dispute Onset: How Legal Uncertainty Drives Maritime Boundary Disputes, Journal of Conflict Resolution 69(7-8), 1172-1204.The Defocalizing Effect of International Courts: Evidence from Maritime Delimitation Practices (with Ezgi Yildiz), Review of International Organizations 20, 825–861.Legal Uncertainty and the Making of Maritime Boundaries. In Uncertainty in Global Politics, eds. Anastasia Shesterinina and Miriam Matejova. London: Routledge, 101–16.Understanding the Limitations of Behaviouralism: Lessons from the Field of Maritime Delimitation (with Ezgi Yildiz), German Law Journal 23(3), 171-195. Resource Disputes in the Eastern Mediterranean. In: Gray K. W. (eds) Global Encyclopedia of Territorial Rights. Springer, Cham.Advanced working papers*International Courts and Selective Restraint in Times of Backlash (with Ezgi Yildiz)When Does ISDS Go Too Far? Arbitration Claim Sensitivity and Reduction of Foreign Investor Protection in International Investment Agreements (with Leopoldo Biffi and Thomas Schultz)*Please feel free to contact me for a copy of the latest drafts.

If you are interested in my work, want to exchange views or collaborate, I would be more than happy to talk to you. teaching.title: Teaching — Umut Yüksel
content:
Graduate-Level Teaching
      

      
        
          “Statistics for International Relations Research I”I have taught the compulsory statistics class (6 ECTS) for Master’s and PhD students in International Relations/Political Science in Fall 2019, 2020, 2021. Find the latest syllabus here.“Introduction to Digital Social Sciences”I have co-taught this class (6 ECTS) in Fall 2021 for the interdisciplinary Master’s programmes at the Geneva Graduate Institute. Find the syllabus here.

Undergraduate Teaching
      

      
        
          "Instruments Matemàtics and Informàtics"I have this compulsory course (4 ECTS) to first-year students enrolled in the program for the Bachelor's degree in Criminology and Public Prevention of Universitat Pompeu Fabra.Find the teaching plan here."Metodologia Quantitativa I"I have this compulsory course (4 ECTS) to first-year students enrolled in the program for the Bachelor's degree in Political and Social Sciences at the Universitat Pompeu Fabra.Find the teaching plan here.

Social Science Methods for International Lawyers
      

      
        
          I have co-designed this methods sequence with the support of the Department of International Law at the Geneva Graduate Institute, and taught or co-taught the following modules:- Fundamentals of Social Science Research- Introduction to Quantitative Data Analysis with R- Basic Quantitative MethodsWe offered this series in Fall 2022 for the European Society of International Law’s Interest Group on Social Sciences and International Law. Find our flyer here.I also taught the sessions on Statistics/Quantitative Methods in 2023, 2024, and 2025.

Other
      

      
        
          I have been an invited lecturer for various classes, teaching basic introductions to qualitative analysis of law as well as survival analysis. I also served as a teaching assistant for four years.

If you are interested in my work, want to exchange views or collaborate, I would be more than happy to talk to you.
